notes.text: Microwave the potatoes 4 at a time, and add 2 minutes for each extra potato in a batch.

move.title: Everything in its place
move.body: Cooks call it mise en place: reading the recipe, then setting out every ingredient before you start. Today the potatoes cook while you set up a topping bar in small bowls, so when they're ready, nothing is left to find or cut.

why.title: Read it all first
why.body: Reading the whole recipe before you start tells you what to do while you wait. Here, the toppings get ready while the potatoes cook.

why.title: One bowl for each
why.body: Small bowls, one for each topping, mean nothing is still being opened, cut, or measured when the hot potatoes come out.

why.title: Prick the skins
why.body: A potato is full of water. As it heats, the water turns to steam. Holes from a fork let the steam out so the potato doesn't burst.

why.title: Microwave, then oven
why.body: The microwave cooks a potato's inside fast but leaves the skin soft. Ten minutes in a hot oven with oil and salt crisps the skin.

why.title: Clean as you go
why.body: Wiping the board and putting things away while the potatoes cook means the kitchen is clean by the time you eat.

wrong.sign: The middle of the potato is still hard
wrong.fix: Microwave it 2 more minutes, then check again with a fork.
Leave it in the oven 5 more minutes.
Cut the potato open sooner, while it's hottest, and push the butter into the middle.

wrong.sign: You're hunting for an ingredient while the potato cools
wrong.fix: Next time, set out every topping before the potatoes finish.

quiz.q: What does mise en place mean?
choices: Everything set out before you start

quiz.q: Why prick the potatoes with a fork?
quiz.explain: Otherwise the steam can burst them.

quiz.q: Why do the potatoes go in the oven after the microwave?
When do you set out the toppings?

steps.text: Read the whole recipe before you start. Then move an oven rack to the middle and heat the oven to 425°F.
steps.tip: Notice what you'll do while the potatoes cook.

steps.text: Scrub the potatoes under running water and dry them with a paper towel.
steps.look: No dirt in the eyes or creases.

steps.text: Poke each potato 6 or 8 times all over with the fork.
steps.tip: Hold the potato on the board, not in your hand, and poke straight down.

steps.text: Set the potatoes on the plate and microwave them. Turn them over with mitts halfway through.
steps.tip: The plate gets hot too. Use mitts.

steps.text: While they cook, put the butter, cheese, and sour cream in small bowls, one each.
steps.look: A row of bowls, one topping in each.

steps.text: Rinse and dry the green onions. Trim off the roots, then slice them thin with the paring knife, claw grip.
Put the green onions in their own small bowl. Set the knife flat at the top of the board.
Mitts on. Push a fork into the thickest potato. It should slide in easily.
steps.look: The fork slides in with no push. If not, microwave 2 more minutes.

steps.text: Move the potatoes to the sheet pan with mitts. Rub them with the oil and sprinkle with the salt.
steps.tip: Use a paper towel to rub on the oil, not your bare hand.

steps.text: Mitts on. Slide the pan into the oven.
While they crisp, wipe the board, put away the cheese bag and sour cream, and rinse the fork.
steps.tip: Clean as you go, and the kitchen is done when dinner is.

steps.text: Mitts on. Pull the rack out, lift out the pan, and set it on the stovetop. Turn off the oven.
Hold a potato with the kitchen towel. Cut a slit along the top with the paring knife, then squeeze the ends to open it.
steps.tip: Steam rushes out. Keep your face back.

steps.text: Top each potato with butter, then cheese, sour cream, green onions, and pepper from the bowls.
steps.look: Butter melting into the middle, cheese softening on top.
